product.amstrad-pc2086.summary: The entry to the PC2000 series retained the 8086 architecture and added integrated VGA for the professional desktop.
product.amstrad-pc2086.history: Announced in September 1988, the PC2086 was the entry to the new professional PC2000 range, below the PC2286 and PC2386. Amstrad offered it for standalone work or as a network workstation. The French price list dated 1 November 1988 priced the PC2086 SD 12 MD, with one floppy drive and a 12-inch monochrome monitor, at 6,590 francs excluding VAT. The April 1989 brochure attributes design to the UK and assembly to Korea, without naming the contractor.
product.amstrad-pc2086.warning: Historical card under research; it does not enable creation of a validated machine in BluMach.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.market: The series targeted professional users. Computerwoche reported its announcement on 30 September 1988; this does not establish the first sale date in each country.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.configu: Buyers could choose according to storage needs. S/SD had one floppy drive, D/DD two, and /30 a 30 MB hard disk alongside a 720 KB drive.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.memory: It retained the basis of first-generation PCs. The brochure and service manual document an 8 MHz 8086, 640 KB of parity RAM and an 8087 socket.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.video: The display did not require an additional card. The brochure documents integrated VGA and compatibility with EGA, CGA and Hercules.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.expansi: Cards could extend the available functions. The brochure, p. 3 and back cover, and service manual, p. 2, specify three 8-bit slots in addition to the hard-disk connection.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.interfa: Printers and communications had dedicated connections. The documentation lists a bidirectional parallel port, RS-232 and a connector for external drives or tape.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.firmwar: The files needed to study startup are preserved. There are two 8 KiB system ROMs, 40179/40180, and a 32 KiB video ROM, 40186, with recorded hashes. Physical chip order still needs checking.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.verifie: BluMach already contains code dedicated to this model. At 88f74ba3, pc2086 and machine_pc2086_init are present; this card review has not tested startup.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.limitat: BluMach's behaviour still needs validation with a reproducible configuration. This card remains under research; FPGA core results do not establish operation in BluMach. A publishable image awaits clear rights.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.brochur: Amstrad PC2000 Series, April 1989, pp. 3, 5 and 7 and back cover: configurations, hardware, assembly and two different slot descriptions.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.prices: Tarifs gamme PC2000, 1 November 1988: indicative French prices excluding VAT, with monitor and configuration specified.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.press: Computerwoche, Amstrad kommt mit PC-Serie 2000, 30 September 1988: announcement and each model's position.
product.amstrad-pc2086.technical.manual: Amstrad PC2086 S/D/30 Service Manual, p. 2: specifications and variants; a copy is preserved with its hash.
